newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe wants quick end to truckers dispute.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe wants quick end to truckers dispute.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe called on Friday for a quick end to a truckers' strike as thousands of lorries blockaded roads across France for a fifth day and sealed off more petrol depots after talks broke down.

"We are aware of the importance of this economic sector for the country and the negotiations must restart quickly and lead to a solution," Juppe told reporters during a visit to Bordeaux, the city of which he is mayor and hardest-hit by the protest.

"Transport Minister Bernard Pons has already done a lot to ensure that dialogue prevails. A solution must be found through talks between haulage bosses and their employees. I hope this will be as soon as possible," Juppe said.
He appeared to reject a demand by union officials that the government participate in the talks and agree to co-finance retirement at 55 instead of 60 for drivers.

About 50,000 trucks were taking part in the protests according to trade unions, and drivers were bent on continuing their action until their demands including wage rises and shorter working hours are met.
Union representatives told reporters they walked out of the negotiations at 2 a.m. (0100 GMT) after nearly 10 hours of talks. But both sides said they hoped to resume talks later in the day.
